meta.location: Moroni's camp, and the land of Nephihah
principles: A request made politely and once

world_behind.title: The chapter sits between two letters
world_behind.text: Alma 56 through 58 is Helaman's epistle. Alma 60 is Moroni's. Verses 1 through 4 are Mormon's account of what Moroni did after reading the first and before writing the second.

world_behind.title: Moroni's first letter to Pahoran is summarized, not quoted
world_behind.text: Verse 3 says he asked that men be gathered to strengthen Helaman. Alma 60:1 confirms it by saying he wrote again.

world_behind.title: Nephihah was founded as a Nephite city
world_behind.text: Alma 50:14 has it built between the cities of Moroni and Aaron. Alma 51:24 has refugees from the city of Moroni fleeing to it.

world_behind.title: The record's account of Nephihah is uneven
world_behind.text: Alma 51:25 says Amalickiah would not let the Lamanites attack it. Alma 51:26 lists it among the cities he took. Alma 59 has Nephites in it and then losing it.

world_behind.title: Nephite dissenters are inside the Lamanite army
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says those driven out of the land of Manti had come over and joined the Lamanites in this part of the land.

world_behind.title: Ammoron is still commanding
world_behind.text: Verse 7 attributes the attack to his order. He has been the Lamanite king since Alma 52:3.

world_behind.title: Moroni's anger arrives at the end
world_behind.text: Verse 13 gives the cause as the government's indifference concerning the freedom of the country. Alma 61 will show that the governor had been driven out of Zarahemla by then.

words.text: Well-being, safety, good condition. The record uses it twenty-one times, first at 2 Nephi 1:25. Moroni's own character is described with it at Alma 48:12, and he will use it three times in his letter in Alma 60, where the tone has changed entirely.

Treated at Alma 54:4, where Ammoron and Moroni trade letters. The word carries a formal, written, and preserved communication. This chapter has Moroni sending one and Alma 60 has him sending a second.

Forced, driven by necessity or by someone else. The record uses it twenty times and applies it in this war block to both sides. Here it describes Nephites who were driven from Manti and then chose the other army.

Under a necessity that leaves no choice. The word occurs seven times in the record and never in the King James Bible. Alma 57:13 used it of Lamanite prisoners; here it describes the survivors of Nephihah.
To hold, keep, and defend. The record uses it forty times, and four of them fall in this chapter alone, at verses 3, 9 twice, and 10. It is the war block's word for keeping ground already won.
Lack of concern or interest. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, as the reason for Moroni's anger. Mormon chose it in preference to a word for malice or treason.

phrases.term: He was exceedingly rejoiced because of the welfare
phrases.text: Moroni's first response to the letter. Helaman had reported hunger, silence from the government, and cities retaken, and Moroni reads the last of those first.
Moroni publishes the good news through the whole region he holds. He treats a report from another front as something the whole army is owed.

phrases.term: He immediately sent an epistle to Pahoran
phrases.text: The action Helaman's letter produces. Moroni asks for men on Helaman's behalf and does not ask for anything for himself.

phrases.term: That he might with ease maintain that part of the land
phrases.text: The stated purpose of the request. Moroni frames reinforcement as a way to hold what has already been won at cost.

phrases.term: He began again to lay a plan
phrases.text: Moroni returns to the offensive while waiting on an answer. The record gives no interval between sending the letter and resuming operations.

phrases.term: Had come over and joined the Lamanites in this part of the land
phrases.text: Nephite dissenters strengthen the army now attacking Nephihah. Mormon has been reporting this pattern since Alma 43:4, and here it shows up as manpower on the day a city falls.

phrases.term: Receiving strength from day to day
phrases.text: The reinforcement Helaman asked for is arriving on the other side. Alma 58:5 said the same thing about the enemy at Manti.

phrases.term: It was easier to keep the city from falling into the hands of the Lamanites than to retake it
phrases.text: The military judgment Moroni holds and the government does not act on. Mormon puts the principle in the middle of the account of the city being lost.

phrases.term: He supposed that they would easily maintain that city
phrases.text: The assumption behind the loss. Moroni expected men to have been sent to Nephihah and planned his own dispositions around that expectation.

phrases.term: He was exceedingly sorrowful, and began to doubt
phrases.text: The strongest personal reaction the record gives Moroni. The doubt is about the people's survival, and verse 11 names its cause as their wickedness.

phrases.term: Moroni was angry with the government
phrases.text: The sentence Alma 60 grows out of. Mormon states the anger plainly and gives the reason in the same breath.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: Good news turns into a requisition in three verses
verses.text: The report of Helaman's recovered lands is received, published to the people so "that they might rejoice also," and converted at once into a request for men. The chapter that ends in anger at the government opens by asking it for something, and the record puts the two only thirteen verses apart.

verses.label: v. 5–7
verses.title: The enemy's reinforcements are the displaced
verses.text: Those who strengthen the Lamanites here are not fresh troops but refugees: "those who had been compelled to flee from the land of Manti, and from the land round about, had come over and joined the Lamanites in this part of the land." The record traces the enemy's growth to a Nephite loss two chapters earlier, and names the commander who uses them.

verses.label: v. 9
verses.title: A sound maxim, and the wrong inference from it
verses.text: The principle is stated as knowledge: "it was easier to keep the city from falling into the hands of the Lamanites than to retake it from them." What follows is stated as assumption, twice over in the same verse — Moroni had supposed men would be sent, and he supposed the city would hold. The record separates what its general knew from what he took for granted, and the second is what fails.

verses.label: v. 10
verses.title: Fourteen words lose a city
verses.text: "Therefore he retained all his force to maintain those places which he had recovered." The decision gets one flat sentence with no deliberation attached, set between a verse of reasoning and a verse of grief. The record spends more on the premise and more on the aftermath than on the choice.

verses.label: v. 13
verses.title: The last verse hands over one word
verses.text: "Moroni was angry with the government, because of their indifference concerning the freedom of their country." Indifference appears once in scripture. A chapter of movements and losses ends on an accusation about a state of mind, and Alma 60 is the letter that follows from it.

chapter.title: A short chapter carries a hinge
chapter.text: Thirteen verses move the war from Helaman's front to Moroni's and set up the exchange of letters that occupies Alma 60 and 61.

chapter.title: The first request is polite
chapter.text: Verse 3 has Moroni asking for men on another commander's behalf, with a stated reason. The letter in Alma 60 will be built on the silence that follows it.

chapter.title: A city is lost to an assumption, and the record says so
chapter.text: Verses 9 and 10 explain that Moroni held his force back because he expected Nephihah to have been garrisoned. Mormon reports the reasoning before reporting the grief.

chapter.title: Both commanders now know the maxim
chapter.text: Keeping a city costs less than retaking it. Helaman learned it at Manti in Alma 58, and Moroni states it here while a city is being lost.

chapter.title: Dissenters are counted as enemy strength
chapter.text: Verse 6 lists the men driven from Manti among those attacking Nephihah. The record keeps treating internal division as a military quantity.

chapter.title: Doubt spreads through the officers
chapter.text: Verse 12 extends Moroni's reaction to all his chief captains. Mormon presents Nephite wickedness as the thing that unsettles them, with Lamanite success as the evidence.

chapter.title: The anger is aimed at indifference
chapter.text: Verse 13 names neither treason nor conspiracy. The word Mormon uses occurs a single time in scripture.

chapter.title: The anger is aimed at men under attack
chapter.text: Alma 61 will report that Pahoran had been driven from Zarahemla by a rebellion. Mormon lets verse 13 stand for a chapter and a half before supplying that.

applications.title: Lead with the good news you were sent
applications.text: Moroni published Helaman's success to everyone in his part of the land. When another team wins, tell your own people about it.

applications.title: Ask for help on someone else's behalf
applications.text: Moroni's request to the governor was for Helaman's army. Advocating for a colleague who is short-handed costs you nothing and may reach further than his own letter did.

applications.title: Expect the displaced to arrive somewhere
applications.text: Those compelled to flee from Manti came over and joined the Lamanites in this quarter of the land. People pushed out of one place do not disappear; they turn up in another, usually carrying a grievance with them.

applications.title: Make room for the people walking away from a loss
applications.text: The remainder of the people of Nephihah fled and joined the army of Moroni. When something collapses near you, the survivors need somewhere to be, and they arrive knowing things you do not.

applications.title: Check the assumption before you act on it
applications.text: Moroni planned around a garrison he had never confirmed. When your plan depends on someone else having done something, verify that they did.

applications.title: Count the reserve you held back
applications.text: Moroni retained all his force to maintain what he had already recovered, which is why nothing went to Nephihah. Keeping everything in reserve is itself a decision about where the risk lands, so make it on purpose.

applications.title: Let the record show the leaders doubted
applications.text: Moroni was sorrowful and began to doubt, and the chapter adds that his chief captains doubted and marveled too. An account in which the people in charge were never shaken is less use to whoever comes after than one that says they were.

applications.title: Name the failure before you decide what caused it
applications.text: Mormon says indifference, and the next two chapters test whether that was the whole story. State what you observed and hold the explanation loosely.

questions.text: Whose success have I been glad to hear about lately?
What good news am I sitting on that others would want?
Who needs me to ask on their behalf?
What has division inside my own group already cost it?
What plan of mine rests on something I have not verified?
What has made me doubt, and what was the actual cause?
Whose indifference makes me angry, and what do I know about their situation?
